task.name: sync failure
task.prompt: I had a sync fail and got the attached error, this needs fixed
task.requirements: fix the error in the image
task.notes: The sync failure came from a duplicate iPod identity that the replacement precheck could miss. hTunes grouped tracks by Title/Artist/Album/TrackNumber but retained only the first record; when that first record was the copy being replaced, a second matching record stayed hidden until Clickwheel rejected the replacement and the whole sync rolled back. IPodSyncService now retains every record in an identity group and explicitly finds a different copy, adopts it, marks the source current, and skips that track before modifying device files. Added a final defensive catch around the replacement Add: if Clickwheel still reports a duplicate, hTunes adopts/skips the surviving copy, restores any missing playlist memberships, counts it as already present, and continues the rest of the batch instead of failing the sync. Added a regression assertion for the first-record-hides-second-duplicate case. Full app and regression-check builds succeeded with zero warnings/errors; all ContextMenuChecks pass. Device write path not runtime-tested because no iPod is available.

task.name: Clicking Sync music Syncs ALL music and replaces everything even stuff that hasnt changed
task.prompt: Clicking Sync music Syncs ALL music and replaces everything even stuff that hasnt changed
task.notes: Root cause: in IPodSyncService.Sync the per-track "does this need copying?" test OR'd the NeedsReplacement heuristic in unconditionally - even for a track whose stored per-device fingerprint exactly matched its current state. NeedsReplacement re-derives format/bitrate/metadata from the device copy and the source file and throws false positives (e.g. a device that reports an empty AlbumArtist, VBR bitrate drift, a path that doesn't resolve), so every unchanged track was re-copied on every "Sync music" run. Fix: the fingerprint is now authoritative. If the track already carries THIS device's last-sync fingerprint and it matches the freshly computed one, the iPod copy is left alone - the only thing that still forces a re-copy in that case is the media file having physically disappeared from the device (new IPodMediaPresent check). NeedsReplacement is still used for legacy/first-time entries that have no stored fingerprint yet, and a changed fingerprint still triggers replacement as before. Extracted the pure check as IPodSyncService.FingerprintMatchesLastSync and covered it in CheckNewStateAndSyncIdentity (never-synced -> not current; matching fingerprint -> current; per-device isolation; edit -> drops out of current). Build clean to builds/debug, all ContextMenuChecks pass. Device write path not runtime-tested (no iPod) but the change only makes the candidate set smaller.

task.name: cancelling sync throws an exception
task.prompt: and ending sync takes forever, also "preparing podcasts" step also takes ages for sync
task.notes: Three problems, all in the sync-cancel path. (1) "Throws an exception": stopping a podcast sync mid-download hit the generic catch in DownloadPodcastEpisodeCoreAsync and popped an "Episode download failed" error dialog, because PodcastService.DownloadEpisodeAsync was called with no CancellationToken and the OperationCanceledException from the aborted HTTP read was treated as a real failure. Fixed: threaded syncToken through DownloadPodcastEpisodeAsync/Core into DownloadEpisodeAsync; Core now rethrows OperationCanceledException instead of showing the failure dialog. StopSync_Click now also swallows ObjectDisposedException if the CTS was disposed by a race. (2) "Ending sync takes forever": on cancel, IPodSyncService.Sync went through its full failure rollback (delete every copied file + restore the iTunesDB) before rethrowing. Now cancellation is cooperative: the copy loop checks IsCancellationRequested between files, breaks, and commits what was copied so far via the normal SaveChanges path. New SyncResult.Cancelled flag; SyncTracksAsync sees it, skips playlist reconciliation, reloads the device list, and shows a "Sync stopped" info dialog (no rollback, no error). PodcastIPodSyncService.Sync gained the same CancellationToken + commit-on-cancel + PodcastSyncResult.Cancelled. (3) "'Preparing podcasts' takes ages": the pre-sync download loop called SavePodcastLibrary + RefreshPodcastShowPanel (which re-decodes the show artwork and refreshes two grids) after every single episode. Added a quiet mode to the download path used by sync: it still saves the JSON for crash safety but skips the per-episode panel refresh, and the sync refreshes the panel once at the end. The loop now reports "Downloading episodes (n/total)" and reacts to Stop immediately. Added CheckSyncCancellationContract to ContextMenuChecks (the Cancelled flag + "Sync stopped." summary prefix for both result types). Build clean, all checks pass. Device write paths not runtime-tested (no iPod) but reuse the existing services' proven patterns.

task.name: podcast icon not showing up during sync
task.prompt: music icon shows up and works fine
task.notes: The H-22 sync animation put the three-glyph assembly at the exact centre of the device strip, so the right-hand (podcast) glyph landed on top of the transcode combo / sync buttons - and the animation Canvas was the first child of its wrapper Grid, i.e. painted BEHIND those opaque controls, so the podcast glyph was hidden. The music glyph (left of centre) sat over the transparent status-text area and showed fine. Fixes: (1) moved the Canvas to be the last child of the wrapper Grid so it paints above the strip content (still IsHitTestVisible=false, so clicks pass through). (2) New AssemblyCentreX(): centres the assembly on the strip but clamps it left so the podcast glyph's right edge stays clear of the transcode combo / SyncCurrent / SyncAll controls (measured live via TransformToVisual), with a floor so it can't run off the left edge on a narrow window. LayoutSyncGlyphs, SyncGlyphCentre and SpawnSyncParticles all use it. Added CheckSyncGlyphPlacement to ContextMenuChecks (asserts the podcast glyph stays left of the combo at 980/1280/1600px and the layer never intercepts clicks). Build clean, all checks pass; verified both music and podcast glyphs render clear of the controls with a throwaway render probe (removed).

task.name: crash when editing tags
task.prompt: the issue is the audio track doesnt exist anymore but its still in the library so it failes
task.requirements: rather than fail the whole process its trying to do just remove it from the library
task.notes: When "Write tags to audio files" was on and a selected track's audio file no longer existed on disk, TagBatchEdit.Apply threw FileNotFoundException in preflight and aborted the entire tag save - no track got tagged. TagBatchEdit.Apply now skips a vanished-file track instead of throwing, collects it, and exposes it via the new TagBatchEdit.MissingFiles property. TagApply_Click drops those stale entries from the library and every playlist (new DropMissingTrackEntries helper), folds the removal into the same undoable "Tag selected tracks" edit, and the status line reports how many tracks were saved vs. removed. Auto-tag (TagAuto_Click) counts a missing-file track as a failure rather than silently no-opping. Library-only edits (write-to-files off) still tag missing-file tracks as before. Updated the ContextMenuChecks TagChecks preflight test to assert the new skip/report/undo contract. Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass.

task.name: sorting issue

task.notes: The podcast episodes DataGrid had its ItemsSource reassigned to a fresh List on every RefreshPodcastShowPanel call, which destroyed the CollectionView holding the user's column sort (so any click-to-sort was wiped on the next refresh). Switched to a persistent ObservableCollection (PodcastEpisodeView) bound once, cleared/repopulated in place - matching the existing VisibleTracks pattern used by the music grid. Column sorting (including Published) now persists across refreshes. Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass.

task.name: download x oldest
task.prompt: download x oldest podcasts doesnt actualy respect the actual age of the podcast episode
task.notes: The per-show "keep X newest/oldest" sync selection ran through PodcastEpisodeOrdering.Order, which sorts by episode number first, then feed position, and only falls back to publish date - so "oldest" picked the lowest episode numbers rather than the genuinely oldest episodes. Added PodcastEpisodeOrdering.ByAge that sorts strictly by PublishedUtc (feed order / episode number only break ties when a feed omits pubDate) and pointed EpisodesForSync at it. The episode grid display still uses Order. Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass.

task.name: audio file not found

task.notes: Auto-tag and music sync previously counted a track whose audio file had vanished from disk as a silent skip/failure and left the stale entry in the library. Added a shared MainWindow.RemoveMissingFilesFromLibrary(missing, context) helper (wrapping the existing DropMissingTrackEntries) that drops such tracks from allTracks and every playlist, records the removal on the undo stack ("Remove N missing files"), logs it, and refreshes the browser. TagAuto_Click now pre-filters the selection through it before the MusicBrainz lookups (and folds in any file that vanishes mid-run), and reports "N removed (missing file)" in the completion summary. SyncTracksAsync drops missing-file entries from the requested set before handing it to IPodSyncService and appends "Removed N tracks with missing files from the library." to the sync summary; this also covers "Sync all". Manual Tag-tab library-only edits still tag missing-file tracks as before (unchanged, still covered by tests). Added CheckMissingFileRemoval to ContextMenuChecks (removal from library + playlists, undo restores both, empty input is a no-op). Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass. task.name: stupid visual idea
task.prompt: could we add a stupid visual thing in the middle of the ipod sync bar we add a ipod icon when we start syncing it fades in, when we stop syncing it fades out to the left a music icon to the right a podcast icon as its syncing one thing or another particles flow from the music or podcast icon into the ipod this continues until the sync finishes
task.notes: Added an ambient sync animation to the device strip (MainWindow.SyncAnimation.cs). A transparent, non-hit-testing Canvas (SyncAnimationLayer) now overlays the DeviceStrip border. It hosts three small muted-blue glyphs centred in the strip: ♫ (music) on the left, ▣ (iPod) in the middle, ◉ (podcast) on the right - matching the app's existing glyph iconography and #44698F accent. StartSyncAnimation(source) fades the iPod glyph plus whichever source glyph applies up to ~0.7-0.85 opacity (QuadraticEase, 320ms) and starts a 110ms DispatcherTimer that spawns 1-2 small Ellipse particles per tick at the source glyph; each particle animates its Canvas.Left/Top toward the iPod glyph over ~0.6-0.9s with an ease-in and fades 0.9->0, removing itself on completion. StopSyncAnimation fades all glyphs back to 0 over 480ms and stops the spawner; in-flight particles finish naturally. Wired into music sync (SyncTracksAsync: start after the sync UI setup, stop in finally) and podcast sync (SyncPodcastSelectionsAsync: same); "Sync all" flows music->podcast so the source glyph swaps mid-run. Timer also stopped on window close. Glyphs re-centre on SizeChanged. Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass; verified the strip layout/rendering with a throwaway RenderTargetBitmap probe (removed).

task.name: tab to select
task.prompt: when we press tab to move to a new text box, and theres already text in the box, automatically hilight all of it so we can override it
task.notes: New TextBoxBehaviors.InstallTabSelectAll() registers a process-wide GotKeyboardFocus class handler for TextBox (called once from the MainWindow constructor, so it also covers the metadata editor, settings and dialog windows). When a text box gains focus while Tab is physically down (i.e. Tab / Shift+Tab moved focus from another control) and it holds text, the whole value is selected on the next input-priority tick so typing overwrites it - matching Windows address-bar behaviour. Guards: skipped for the initial focus when a window opens (e.OldFocus null), read-only or disabled boxes, multi-line (AcceptsReturn) boxes like the download links box, empty boxes, and cases where the user already moved the caret or inline autocomplete kept focus (SelectionLength check + IsKeyboardFocused re-check). Mouse clicks are unaffected (Tab not held). Decision logic factored into the testable ShouldSelectAllOnFocus; covered by CheckTabSelectAll in ContextMenuChecks. Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass.

task.name: rate-limit
task.prompt: also im being rate limited by music brainz, im not sure why, maybe we should add more info to the fial/success info?
task.notes: Root cause of the rate-limiting: the throttle timestamp was recorded only after each response returned and a single auto-tag lookup fires 1-2 requests, so bursts slipped under the 1s window and MusicBrainz answered 503, which surfaced only as a generic "failed". Fixes: GetJsonAsync now stamps the timestamp at request start (true request-to-request spacing), widened to 1200ms, and on 503/429 it honours the Retry-After header and retries up to 2x before throwing a typed MusicBrainzRateLimitException. Auto-tag now counts rate-limit hits separately, shows a live "Paused on X" status with a cool-down, and the completion summary explains the ~1 req/sec limit and surfaces the last error instead of a bare count. Build clean, ContextMenuChecks pass.
